first_section.title: About Us
first_section.subtitle: Platzhirsch Home Living – your design furniture studio in Vorarlberg, Austria
first_section.text: Welcome to Platzhirsch Home Living, your interior studio for designer furniture and considered living concepts on Lake Constance. In our showroom in Lochau near Bregenz – Landstraße 11, just minutes from the German and Swiss borders – you will find international design brands, interior design and personal interior advice. What defines us is a love of timeless design and fine craftsmanship: every piece of furniture, every light and every accessory in our exhibition is carefully chosen. Our team accompanies you from the first idea through planning to delivery and installation – whether it is a single favourite piece, a complete home or an ambitious interior design project. Get to know us, explore our brands and take a seat. We look forward to welcoming you in Vorarlberg, Austria.

ausstellung.headline: Inspiration is where every interior begins.
ausstellung.desc: Every new interior starts with gathering inspiration – and that is why we created our showroom on Lake Constance. On our exhibition floor in Lochau we show living ideas and pieces from our furniture brands such as Minotti, Poliform, Rimadesio, ClassiCon, Flos, Eichholtz, Paola Lenti and Tréca. Selected accessories, wall paints, wallpapers and rugs complete the range. You are welcome to sit and lie down on the pieces – at your own pace and with personal advice.
ausstellung.careerTitle: Meet the people behind Platzhirsch Home Living.
ausstellung.tourDesc1: Step into the world of Platzhirsch Home Living and experience our furniture studio in Lochau from the comfort of your home. With our virtual 360° tour you can explore our exhibition, stylish designer furniture and inspiring interior concepts – anytime, from anywhere.
ausstellung.tourDesc2: Move freely through our carefully designed spaces, take a close look at our design highlights and feel the particular atmosphere of our studio on Lake Constance. Whether you are looking for new interior ideas, want a preview of our collections or simply seek inspiration – the 360° tour is a good introduction to your visit in Vorarlberg, Austria.

einblicke.description: Our own heatmap: where people click, scroll and drop off. No third party, no recording, no input.
einblicke.purpose: We want to understand how our pages are used and improve them. We only record: click position and clicked element, mouse movement in a coarse 40 px grid (desktop only), scroll depth, viewing time per section, the names of form fields you touched (never their content, no keystrokes), validation and script errors (type only), goals reached such as an appointment or enquiry, steps in our planners, the traffic channel (e.g. “Organic”), the device group and the window width. There is no session recording, no IP address, no fingerprinting and no disclosure to third parties. A random session ID stays in your browser's sessionStorage for 30 minutes. We delete raw data after 14 days at the latest; after that only summarised daily figures (at least 5 visits per page) remain in our own back office. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are respected.

paragraphs: In our showroom, pieces by different manufacturers stand side by side, just as they might later stand in your home. We plan dimensions, upholstery and materials with you and take care of delivery and installation.

For living and dining we plan with upholstery by Minotti, Bullfrog and Papadatos, tables and chairs by Desalto and Tonon, and classics by ClassiCon. Rimadesio and Poliform add wardrobe systems, room dividers and glass doors.
For kitchens and bathrooms we show next125, Schüller and Frost as well as antoniolupi and Agape. Outdoors we plan with Gloster, Paola Lenti, Solpuri, Sifas, EMU, Tuuci, Umbrosa and Heatsail.

Lighting comes from Flos, Tom Dixon, Brand van Egmond and Quasar. Tréca stands for beds, Trapa for wooden floors, and Eichholtz, Lambert, Pomax, Qeeboo, 101 Copenhagen, Baobab and Alonpi for accessories and textiles.
Ask us beforehand which pieces are currently on display in Lochau.

items.q: How does an interior consultation at Platzhirsch work?
items.a: We get to know you and your rooms, at the studio in Lochau or at your place if you wish. Harald Menghin first draws your concept by hand and builds a room model where it helps; then we plan in 3D and show you the room photorealistically.

items.q: Where does the consultation take place?
items.a: At our studio with café at Landstraße 11, 6911 Lochau on Lake Constance. If needed, we come to you and look at rooms, light and surroundings on site.
Whatever you have: floor plan, photos and room dimensions. We clarify everything else together.
{hours}. Appointments outside opening hours by arrangement.

items.q: What is the difference between interior advice and interior design?
items.a: With interior advice we choose furniture, lighting, fabrics and colours for existing rooms with you. With interior design, Harald Menghin draws the whole room concept by hand, with a room model and 3D planning. Where structure, building services or planning permission are involved, we work with your architect and the specialist planners.

That depends on the scope, from advice for one room to a whole house with hand drawing, model and 3D planning. We discuss how your project is charged with you in advance; you receive a quote on request.

items.q: How long does it take from sketch to delivery?
items.a: Mainly on the manufacturers’ delivery times, which differ by brand, model and finish. We set the schedule together after the planning, before anything is ordered.

haltung.title: We are designers. We take our time.
haltung.p1: With us, a furnishing project does not start in a catalogue but with you: your rooms, your light and your everyday life.
haltung.p2: That is why we come to you. If your project needs it, we also stay on site for a day or two.
haltung.p3: What we see there, Harald Menghin draws by hand. The drawing becomes a model, the model an exact 3D plan. So the first idea stays intact until the finished room.

stepTexts.s1: We talk in the showroom in Lochau, over a coffee in the café, or at your home. You tell us how you live and what should change. Floor plans, photos and measurements help but are not required.
stepTexts.s2: A room is more than its floor plan. We look at how the light moves during the day, how the room feels in summer and in winter and which paths you take every day. If your project needs it, we stay for a day or two.
stepTexts.s3: Harald Menghin sketches floor plans, perspectives and moods by hand. On paper, variants can be compared quickly, and you see early where things are heading. The drawing does not show every detail, but the idea.
stepTexts.s4: Then Harald builds a scale model of the room, as architects and developers do. You can touch it, look at it from all sides and rearrange it together with us. Many questions are settled faster at the table than on a screen.
stepTexts.s5: We transfer drawing and model into a digital plan with exact dimensions and the selected products and materials. Now it shows whether every door opens, every drawer fits and every sofa passes through the stairwell.
stepTexts.s6: The plan becomes a photorealistic image of your room. You see how fabrics, wood and light work together before anything is ordered. You give feedback in conversation or in the customer portal, also by voice message.
stepTexts.s7: We order, coordinate delivery and, on request, installation. If several trades are involved, we coordinate the dates. And we stay with your project until everything stands as it was drawn.

harald.text: Harald thinks with a pencil. Before he plans on screen, he draws. Then he builds the model you keep working on with us. He accompanies your project from the first sketch to the plan.

q1.q: Does Harald really draw every concept by hand?
q1.a: Yes, our furnishing concepts start with a hand drawing, and then Harald builds a model. How many sketches and how detailed the model becomes depends on the project. We discuss this in the first appointment.

q2.q: Why a model when there are 3D renderings?
q2.a: You can pick up a model and rearrange it together. Many questions about proportions and paths are settled faster this way. The 3D plan follows and makes everything exact.

q3.q: Do you come to my home?
q3.a: Yes. We look at your rooms on site, in Vorarlberg, around Lake Constance and in the neighbouring regions. If your project needs it, we stay a day or two to understand light, climate and routines.

q4.q: What does planning with hand drawing and model cost?
q4.a: That depends on the scope. In the first appointment we clarify what your project needs. We discuss the costs with you before we continue planning.

q5.q: When will I see what my room will look like?
q5.a: The hand drawing already shows the idea. With the photorealistic rendering you see your room with materials and light before anything is ordered.

q6.a: Yes, at every step. At the model, in conversation or in the customer portal, also by voice message.

care.title: Every material needs its own care
care.text: This is what Gloster, one of the outdoor brands we carry, recommends in its care sheets. For furniture by other manufacturers we follow their care instructions.

teak.name: Teak
points: Untreated teak turns silver grey over time. According to Gloster this takes 6 months to 2 years, depending on the location.
Clean thoroughly once or twice a year with water and a mild detergent.
Never use a pressure washer: it roughens the soft surface.
Store dry over the winter, but do not move it straight into a heated room. Sharp changes in temperature and humidity can cause splits.

aluminium.name: Powder-coated aluminium
points: Wipe with water and a mild liquid detergent, using a microfibre cloth or sponge.
Then dry it with a cloth to avoid water spots.
No abrasive cleaners: they can mark the powder coat. According to Gloster, damage to the coating is very difficult to repair invisibly.

rope.name: Rope
points: First brush off loose dirt gently.
Clean with a mild solution, according to Gloster 1 part detergent to 16 parts lukewarm water below 40 °C, with a sponge or soft brush.
Rinse thoroughly until no soap is left in the rope and let it air dry.

wicker.name: Wicker
points: According to the manufacturer, Gloster's synthetic wicker can stay outside all year, from −20 °C to +55 °C. Storage protects it from leaves, dirt and algae.
Clean with a mild solution and a soft brush, rinse with cold water.
Remove all foam residue: otherwise it attracts dirt in the gaps. Do not spray teak parts with pressure.

fabrics.name: Outdoor fabrics and cushions
points: According to Gloster, cover cushions or store them dry when not in use.
Remove dirt before it becomes embedded and blot spills straight away.
The covers of most Gloster cushions are not meant to be removed. Cleaning is done on the cushion.

meta.title: Gaggenau, Miele, BORA & Quooker appliances | Platzhirsch
meta.description: Gaggenau, Miele, V-ZUG, BORA, Liebherr and Quooker at Platzhirsch in Lochau: planned into your kitchen, delivered and installed.

kuechengeraete.title: Built-in appliances from Gaggenau to Quooker
kuechengeraete.lead: Oven, hob, cooling, dishwashing and water are part of the plan from the start. You can get appliances from Gaggenau, Miele, V-ZUG, BORA, Liebherr and Quooker through us – planned into your kitchen, delivered and installed from one source.

marken.title: Selected for planning
marken.text: Which appliances suit your kitchen depends on how you cook and how the room is used. We supply appliances from these brands and match them to fronts, niches and connections in the plan.

gaggenau.text: Ovens, steam ovens, hobs and wine climate cabinets from Germany. We plan them so that heights, gaps and fronts match the rest of the kitchen.

miele.text: Built-in appliances from Germany, from the dishwasher to the steam oven. In the plan we pay attention to working heights, walkways and the space around the sink.

vzug.text: Steam ovens, ovens and refrigerators from Switzerland. We agree niches, connections and operating height together with you.

bora.text: Hobs with integrated extraction that draws the vapour downwards. The space above the hob stays free – this changes how we plan the island and the wall cabinets.

liebherr.text: Refrigerators, freezers and wine climate cabinets. We decide with you whether they disappear behind furniture fronts or stay deliberately visible, and plan space and ventilation.

quooker.text: A tap from the Netherlands that delivers boiling water alongside cold and hot. We plan the space in the base cabinet and the connection.

ablauf.title: Technology that fits the design
ablauf.step1Text: We ask how you cook, how many people eat with you and what matters to you day to day. This shows which appliances belong in your kitchen.
ablauf.step2Text: Harald Menghin first draws your kitchen by hand: walkways, work triangle, storage and light – and the space for every appliance.
ablauf.step3Text: The 3D plan adds exact dimensions and connections. We deliver and install appliances and kitchen from one source.
ablauf.kueche: The appliances fit into the kitchens we plan – for example from next125 (Schüller) or Poliform.
ablauf.tausch: Keeping your kitchen but replacing an appliance? We also supply and install appliances from these brands on their own – for example as a replacement in your existing kitchen. Just bring the niche dimensions or your current model.
ablauf.schauraum: Our showroom in Lochau has several display kitchens with appliances from some of these brands. We are happy to tell you before your visit which ones you will see there.
ablauf.armaturen: We plan kitchen taps by Dornbracht into the design.

facts.title: At a glance
facts.whoText: {name} is an interior design studio for designer furniture with its own café in the house. It is run by {legalName}.
facts.whereText: {address}, on Lake Constance between Bregenz and Lindau.
facts.minottiLink: Minotti press release on the opening
facts.servicesText: Interior planning by hand with a room model, 3D planning and rendering; kitchens with built-in appliances; bathroom and wellness; outdoor; hotel and contract; yacht interiors. Delivery and installation on request.

items.q: Is there a café in the house?
items.a: Yes. The {cafe}, our own café, is in the same house at Landstraße 11. It has its own opening hours ({cafeHours}) and the phone number {cafePhone}.

items.q: In which languages do you advise?
items.a: We advise in German, English, Italian and French. Just tell us your preferred language when you request an appointment.

items.q: Where is the Minotti Studio by Platzhirsch Home Living?
items.a: In our house at Landstraße 11, 6911 Lochau, on Lake Constance between Bregenz and Lindau. Minotti opened the studio itself; the source is linked under “At a glance”.
You are welcome to drop in during opening hours ({hours}). For planning we take our time by appointment; appointments outside opening hours by arrangement.

items.q: Which saunas and spa elements do you plan?
items.a: With Starpool we plan saunas, steam baths and experience showers, with Soleum and Fabio Alemanno heated loungers and hammam tables. What suits your room depends on space, ventilation and connections; we clarify this on site.

items.q: What does a hot tub need indoors or in the garden?
items.a: A level base that can carry the load, a power connection and room for maintenance and the cover. Aquavia Spa makes models for indoors and outdoors, built-in or with overflow; care and water treatment follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

items.q: Which trades does a private spa at home need?
items.a: Usually an electrician, a plumber, ventilation or building services and a tiler. We plan the room, routes and connections by hand and in 3D and coordinate delivery and installation with the trades.

items.q: Which brands are you a dealer for?
items.a: {markenSatz} We also plan bathroom pieces by Agape with you.

items.q: Gaggenau or Miele: what changes in the planning?
items.a: Planning is mainly about installation dimensions, niche heights, connected loads and how the appliances sit next to each other; these figures differ by series and manufacturer. We fix the appliances in the hand drawing and the 3D plan before the kitchen is ordered.

items.q: Do you also fit appliances into an existing kitchen?
items.a: Yes, we also deliver and install single appliances, for example as a replacement. Whether an appliance fits without alterations depends on the niche, connections and ventilation; bring the dimensions or the old model.

items.q: Do you deliver and install in Germany and Switzerland too?
items.a: Delivery and installation are available on request, also for projects in Germany and Switzerland. Deliveries to Switzerland involve customs and Swiss VAT; we clarify this before you order.
